title: The Rare-Earth Game
content: China will probably not impose a rare-earth embargo, but it will keep the specter of one alive. And the West will probably not achieve self-sufficiency in this critical sector, but it will keep seeking to reduce its vulnerability to a supply shock through expensive capacity duplication and stockpiles.

title: Why Research Matters
content: Over the past 21 months, in the country that has leveraged research to greatest effect, the government is slashing funding for it, closing centers where it is done, politicizing grant-making decisions, and bullying its single biggest engine: universities. The costs will be far greater than many realize.

title: Africa Needs a Different Kind of Climate Finance
content: Roughly half of the climate finance that flows to Africa comes in the form of debt, with multilateral and bilateral development-finance institutions often lending at commercial rates to economies already struggling to carry the added costs. To maximize fiscal space, the instruments used to deliver climate finance need to change.

title: Effective Climate Action Requires Capable States
content: With delegations from around the world gathering for another international climate conference, the question today is not whether governments should do more to address the climate crisis, but whether they even have the capabilities to do so. After 40 years of free-market orthodoxy, many simply do not.

title: Why Is Mexico Defying Latin America’s Right Turn?
content: How Mexico’s left has managed to retain strong support is a key question of contemporary Latin American politics. The most likely answer centers on the ruling Morena party’s pragmatic brand of left-wing politics, which combines bold redistributive policies, greater security, and a willingness to compromise in the name of both.

But while the Federal Reserve and other central banks have shelved their plans, the European Central Bank is pressing ahead with its digital euro.

title: Medical AI Needs Bedside Manners
content: Even the most accurate medical AI tools have little value if they make patients uneasy or doctors find them too cumbersome. A comfort-by-design approach could overcome these obstacles by involving patients and practitioners in development and ensuring that new systems work with existing medical practices.

content: Europe is racing to expand its AI data-center capacity, but its power grids are already strained, and local communities are increasingly pushing back against new construction. Achieving technological sovereignty will require less grandstanding and more practical solutions that make better use of existing resources.

Private companies should not have the power to decide unilaterally which risks the public will bear.
